summary: 2026 ops consoles have converged on a single, calm shell: a collapsible-to-icons sidebar with flat label-only groups and an org switcher in its header, a sticky page action bar carrying breadcrumbs, tabs and a visible ⌘K trigger, and a command palette that has grown from navigation into a context-aware action surface. Data surfaces are built as two primitives (clickable list rows for streams, true grid tables for comparable numbers) with named density modes, tabular numerals, mono scoped to identifiers, and row detail in a resizable right panel, while workflow entities keep full pages and destructive actions get stakes-proportional confirmation. Visually the dialect is restraint: OKLCH-authored two-layer tokens with a tinted neutral shared across products and only the accent varying, separately tuned dark scales, hairline alpha borders with shadows reserved for floating layers, 4-8px radii, 13px body with 12px labels, a branded sans+mono pair, and 16px/1.5px stroke icons, all frozen in tokens and lint rules to resist the generic AI-template look.

decisions.decision: Ship one single-tier shadcn Sidebar (SidebarProvider collapsible="icon", variant="inset") at 240px expanded / 48px icon rail, toggled by Cmd/Ctrl+B and SidebarRail hover, state persisted in a cookie (sidebar_state) so first paint matches, with Tooltip labels on every icon-only item and SidebarMenuSkeleton while nav data loads.
decisions.because: Collapsible-to-icons sidebars with persisted state are now table stakes: shadcn ships it as the default template with cmd/ctrl+B and cookie persistence; Vercel's Jan-Feb 2026 redesign replaced tabs with a hideable resizable sidebar; Atlassian's Dec 2025 full-height sidebar added Ctrl+[ because the collapse button was hard to find; Supabase (Feb 2025) and Grafana (localStorage docked state) persist the preference; NN/g's caveat that icon rails only work for daily-use apps holds for a developer/ops audience. Sentry's two-tier rail (74px + 190px panel) is built for a multi-product suite; ~20 latchkey sections cluster into 6 groups and fit one tier.

decisions.decision: Cap the sidebar at two levels: a per-user Pinned group (SidebarGroup + SidebarMenuAction pin/unpin, seeded per role, plus a 5-item Recent list) at the top, then 5-6 task-oriented groups with non-interactive SidebarGroupLabel headers (11px, uppercase, tracking-wide, text-muted-foreground, 16px gap between groups) and 28px SidebarMenuButton rows (size="sm", 13px text); no SidebarMenuSub accordions, and each entity's sub-pages become tabs in the page action bar. latchkey groups: Directory (Identities, Sessions, Invitations), Access (Clients, Grants, Scopes), Tenancy (Tenants, Organizations), Security (Policies, Audit), Settings; tripline: Issues, Performance, Releases, Alerts, Settings; runsheet: Runbooks, Runs, Incidents, Settings.
decisions.because: Auth0's Sept 2026 dashboard refresh (an IdP with essentially latchkey's section count) moved to label-only group headers and six task-oriented sections; GitLab Pajamas (July 2026) states there is no third nav level; Grafana Saga sends level 4 to page tabs; Primer pairs NavList with UnderlineNav and breadcrumbs. Pinned/starred layers are established at Linear (Dec 2024 hide/reorder/More), Sentry Issue Views (June 2025 starred views in nav), Grafana Bookmarks (11.2) and GitLab (seeded default pins), and reduce traversal of a long IA without hiding it.

decisions.decision: Put one shared OrgSwitcher (shadcn sidebar-07 TeamSwitcher pattern: 24px avatar + org name + chevron in a DropdownMenu inside SidebarHeader, collapsing to the avatar button in icon mode) in all three apps, move the personal account menu to the top-right of the page action bar, and treat the next scope level as a page-header filter rather than a second sidebar: tripline project/environment selector, latchkey active-tenant selector, runsheet team/service selector, all encoded as /o/:org/... with ?tenant= / ?project= query state so the nav shape never changes.
decisions.because: One org in view at a time, switched from the sidebar header, is near-universal (Vercel team switcher top-left, Supabase Feb 2025 org-at-a-time with account menu moved top-right, Sentry OrganizationDropdown in SidebarHeader, GitLab 2023 context header, Clerk OrganizationSwitcher, shadcn sidebar-07). Vercel's 2026 redesign uses 'projects as filters' with the same tabs at team and project level and Sentry uses a global project/env filter bar, which avoids the separate-sidebar-per-scope complexity Supabase and GitLab carry.

decisions.decision: Standardise a sticky 48px (h-12) PageActionBar in the shared shell with four slots: SidebarTrigger + vertical Separator, router-derived Breadcrumb (org > scope > resource > detail, every crumb a real landing page), a Tabs slot for per-entity views (Overview / Sessions / Grants / Audit on a latchkey client; Events / Tags / Activity on a tripline issue), and a right-aligned actions slot that always contains a visible '⌘K Search…' input chip (h-8, w-56) plus the account menu.
decisions.because: GitHub (GA Oct 2023) made IA-reflecting breadcrumbs the hierarchy indicator; Auth0's Sept 2026 refresh introduced exactly a sticky page action bar with breadcrumbs, tabs, actions and the sidebar toggle; Grafana Saga generates crumbs from page structure and requires every nav entry to have a landing page; shadcn's sidebar-07/08 blocks render SidebarTrigger + Separator + Breadcrumb by default. GitHub's July 2025 palette deprecation-and-reversal showed an undiscoverable palette reads as unused, so practitioners recommend a visible ⌘K chip in the header.

decisions.decision: Build one shared CommandDialog (shadcn Command on cmdk, ⌘K, on by default, no feature flag) fed by a per-app registry with three sources: static pages for every nav section (so it is useful on day one), async entity search (tripline: issue/event/trace ID, release; latchkey: identity by email, session ID, client_id, tenant slug; runsheet: runbook name, incident) and context-aware actions that appear when rows are selected (bulk resolve/assign/archive in tripline; revoke session, resend invitation, rotate secret as stepwise flows in latchkey; start run / mark step in runsheet); keep ⌘B for the sidebar, support Backspace to pop nested pages and paste-an-internal-URL to jump, and log palette usage from launch.
decisions.because: Sentry's June 2026 Cmd+K upgrade turned the palette into an action bus (bulk archive/resolve/assign, only the next valid step shown); Linear added Settings navigation and internal-URL paste in July 2025; Vercel's Geist CommandMenu guidance codifies nested pages, verb-phrase commands and grouping past ~30 items; Grafana, Langfuse and Novu all added ⌘K menus; GitHub's July 2025 reversal after 'low usage' on an opt-in palette is the warning to ship it on by default and measure.

decisions.decision: Ship one DataTable wrapper on TanStack Table v9 (useTable + tableFeatures) with TanStack Virtual under the shadcn Table, exposing density as a data-density="compact|normal|spacious" attribute on the table root that sets --cell-py 4px/8px/12px and --cell-px 8px/12px/16px (28/36/44px rows on 12-13px type, 20px line-height), chosen from a view-options menu and persisted per route in localStorage; defaults: tripline issue list compact, latchkey entity lists normal with a compact toggle, runsheet run history normal. Sizing regimes: client-held sets (stack frames, breadcrumbs, spans, events-for-one-issue) virtualise with fixed row height per density; server-backed lists cursor-paginate at 25-50 rows with 'Previous / Next' and '21–40 of 142' copy and a page-size selector; live streams (runsheet run logs, tripline live events) append behind an 'N new' pill rather than auto-scroll.
decisions.because: Primer DataTable's cellPadding condensed/normal/spacious (4/8/12px block padding) is the reference density implementation and its ListViewDensityToggle persists to localStorage; GitHub Projects (June 2026) and Grafana 12.x expose row height in view options; Datadog Events offers compact-to-expanded density; Vercel design.md limits compact density to dense lookup. Grafana rebuilt its table on a virtualised grid (GA Sept 2025, 41k-row benchmark) and disables virtualisation for dynamic height; Geist Table exposes virtualize plus Previous/Next range copy; Polaris paginates past 50-100 rows; Vercel Runtime Logs uses 'Show New Logs' instead of infinite scroll; shadcn's data-table guide targets TanStack v9.

decisions.decision: Provide two row primitives on the same tokens (row height per density, hover bg via alpha neutral, 2px inset focus ring): a ListRow (whole row clickable, primary text + inline 12px muted metadata + status glyph + trailing hover actions) for tripline's issue stream and runsheet run/incident history, and the grid DataTable for tripline p50/p95 tables and latchkey identities/sessions/clients/grants. In the grid: numeric columns and their headers get text-right + tabular-nums (including placeholders and totals), identifiers (session/client/tenant IDs, request IDs, SHAs, ISO timestamps, JWKS kid) render via a shared <Id> component in font-mono at 12.5px, empty values render '—' never 'N/A', times are relative ('5h ago') within 7 days then absolute ('Mar 14, 2026') via shared formatters, headers are Title Case nouns like 'Requests (7d)'.
decisions.because: Primer keeps ListView (primary info + metadata + actions) separate from DataTable, which is reserved for flat comparable 2-D data; Geist says use Table only when at least one column is sortable/comparable; Sentry's 2025 issue stream made the whole row clickable with a few aligned columns. Primer's guideline 'right-align numeric values and use tabular-num' and Vercel design.md's 'set only the identifier in Mono, not its sentence or entire table', em dash for unknowns and 7-day relative-to-absolute rule are the codified house rules; Polaris s-table-header format="numeric" does the same; Tailwind v4 ships tabular-nums natively.

decisions.decision: Make sticky structure a table-level option in the shared DataTable: header sticky inside the table's own overflow container (not the window), TanStack column pinning with position: sticky for the primary identifier column on the left and the row-actions (DropdownMenu ellipsis) column on the right, z-index tokens (--z-table-header 10, --z-sticky-col 5) shared with the shell so headers never fight the sidebar or PageActionBar; enable it by default on latchkey tables with 8+ columns and tripline transaction tables, off for runsheet. Status inside cells is never colour-only: a StatusDot renderer (6px dot + text under a real column header) for latchkey session active/revoked, invitation pending/accepted, client enabled/disabled, a Level renderer (16px icon + text) for tripline error/warning/info and runsheet ok/failed/skipped, Badge reserved for tags/labels/environments only, and a subtle left-border or bg tint (--danger-muted) on fatal/5xx rows.
decisions.because: Grafana's table GA (Sept 2025) added frozen leading columns as a user option; Polaris DataTable fixedFirstColumns and IndexTable lastColumnSticky are the design-system convention for a sticky trailing actions column; TanStack documents left/right pinning with sticky CSS in one table; Setproduct warns misaligned sticky columns are worse than none. Primer StateLabel pairs every status with an icon and requires a column header, Vercel design.md rejects pills for ordinary metadata and tints 4xx amber / 5xx red at row level in Runtime Logs, Grafana 12.2 scoped a dedicated Pill cell type to tag-like values, and Carbon's status pattern requires symbol+colour+text.

decisions.decision: Adopt a split rule for detail surfaces: hub/workflow entities (tripline issue; latchkey identity, tenant, client; runsheet runbook) get full pages with progressive disclosure (a right-hand meta column plus drawers for tags/breadcrumbs/audit), while row-level records (tripline events/spans/breadcrumbs; latchkey sessions, grants, invitations, audit rows; runsheet run steps) open in one shared DetailSheet (shadcn Sheet side="right", resizable 400-720px with width remembered, route-synced via ?panel=<id> so links are shareable, ↑/↓ or j/k moves between rows, an 'Open full page' escape hatch). The Sheet is never used for create/edit forms (those are pages) or destructive confirmations (those are Dialogs).
decisions.because: Grafana 12.3 logs and Logs Drilldown open details in a resizable right sidebar with ↑/↓ row navigation; Datadog Log Explorer, Vercel Runtime Logs (URL-shareable) and GitHub Projects use the same side panel; Sentry's Issue Details redesign (default since 2 Mar 2026) keeps the issue as a page with drawers; Linear Peek established Space/arrow preview. Primer's Dialog guidance restricts side sheets to quick previews and global actions ('use a page' for create/edit), Geist Modal says drawers read too soft for delete/revoke, and Atlassian is deprecating Drawer entirely.

decisions.decision: Encode a three-tier mutation contract in the shell that each app maps its actions onto: tier 1 optimistic (React 19 useOptimistic) with an 8s Undo toast for frequent reversible actions (tripline resolve/assign/mute/archive, runsheet mark-step-done, latchkey enable/disable client); tier 2 a Dialog with focus defaulting to Cancel, a verb+noun destructive primary ('Revoke session', 'Delete runbook'), Enter never confirming; tier 3 the same Dialog gated on a typed resource name for delete tenant, remove grant, rotate client secret, delete project. Pair it with feedback rules: Toast (Sonner/shadcn, aria-live polite) only for acknowledgments; every failure or actionable state renders as a persistent inline Note/InlineMessage or field error; declarative forms (client/tenant settings, runbook step notes) use explicit Save with no autosave mixed in, imperative controls (toggles, status/assignee selects) autosave with an inline 'Saved' indicator; a shared EmptyState with named variants no-results / blank-slate / cleared / permission / error, with latchkey's RBAC-denied routes rendering the full-page permission variant and tripline's fresh project showing the blank-slate variant with the DSN/SDK snippet.
decisions.because: Vercel's Web Interface Guidelines and Geist Toast/Modal codify optimistic updates with a 5-10s Undo window, Cancel-focused destructive modals with no Enter-to-confirm, and typed-name gates for high-stakes targets; Primer Saving prescribes explicit save for declarative inputs, autosave for imperative controls, never mixed, and inline/banner success over toasts; Geist Toast bars toasts as the sole channel for failures the user must triage; Geist Empty State and Primer Blankslate key variants to why the space is empty and require a next step ('no dead ends').

decisions.decision: Keep the shadcn semantic contract as the only public API but generate it from a Radix-style 12-step scale layer authored in OKLCH (Tailwind v4 @theme + color-mix(in oklab) for alpha): one shared tinted neutral for all three consoles (shadcn baseColor 'mauve', Radix mauve, chroma ≈0.005-0.01 so status hues still pop), dedicated status scales with fixed hues added to the contract from day one (--success/--success-foreground green, --warning amber, --info blue, alongside the existing --destructive red, each with -muted background and -border steps), a separate chart-1..5 categorical set so a green line never implies 'ok', and the accent as the only per-app variable delivered as three shadcn presets: tripline violet, runsheet indigo, latchkey blue, each also driving --sidebar-primary / --sidebar-accent so the org-switcher shell is recognisable per product. Components may reference only semantic tokens, never scale steps (lint rule).
decisions.because: Tailwind v4 and shadcn's Tailwind v4 release moved the whole palette to OKLCH; Radix (12 steps with fixed roles), Geist (10x10), Primer (base -> functional -> component), Atlassian and Sentry's SCRAPS theme (Nov 2025, background/border/content x neutral/accent/promotion/danger/warning/success) all layer semantic roles over fixed-role scales and remap them for dark; Primer, Atlassian and Sentry separate accent from status roles and Radix recommends dedicated error/success/warning/info scales; shadcn ships only destructive and documents adding --warning; Radix Themes auto-pairs a tinted gray to the accent for dense text-heavy UIs and shadcn's 2026 presets encode baseColor separately from theme; Linear generates 98+ variables from base+accent+contrast, which is the 'three presets of one theme' shape.

decisions.decision: Tune the dark theme as its own scale rather than an inversion: a lifted, mauve-tinted near-black base (--background ≈ oklch(0.16 0.008 300), Sentry's #0D0A10 territory), elevation by lighter surfaces (card +1 step, popover +2 steps) with shadows as a secondary cue, alpha neutrals for hover/selected rows (--row-hover white/6%, --row-selected accent/12%; black/4% and accent/8% in light) so they work on card, popover and sidebar alike, color-scheme set on <html> via .dark and a matching theme-color meta. Structure comes from hairline alpha borders (--border black/8% light, white/10% dark; --border-soft at half that for row dividers), shadows only on floating layers (tooltip lightest, menu 'lift', dialog/toast 'further lift', each paired with a semi-transparent border), shadow-xs at most on resting controls, a 3px --ring focus ring, and a small concentric radius scale (--radius 0.375rem: 6px controls/badges/inputs, 8px cards/popovers, 12px menus/dialogs, never rounded table rows or sidebar items past 6px). Defaults: tripline and runsheet dark-led with a system option, latchkey system/light; the sidebar is one step dimmer than the content pane in both themes so the 20-section nav recedes.
decisions.because: Primer, Atlassian (raised/overlay surfaces lighter in dark mode because shadows are hard to see), Sentry SCRAPS (distinct dark primitives, transparent.* tokens) and Geist/Radix alpha scales all treat dark as a separately tuned scale with alpha overlays; Vercel's guidelines require color-scheme: dark on <html> and semi-transparent borders combined with two-layer shadows; Linear's Mar 2026 refresh dimmed the sidebar and lowered separator contrast ('structure should be felt not seen'); Tailwind v4 shifted radius scales down and made border color explicit; Geist materials pin 6px controls / 12px menus and modals and Linear uses 6/8/12px only; Grafana, Linear and Vercel are dark-led while GitHub, Atlassian and Shopify admin default light.

decisions.decision: Self-host Geist Sans + Geist Mono (geist npm package) as --font-sans / --font-mono in the Tailwind v4 @theme with font-feature-settings 'tnum' available via tabular-nums and 'zero' (slashed zero) plus ligatures off on the mono; set the scale in rem at 12/13/14/16 with 13px (0.8125rem) as the app body size and table row text, 12px for SidebarGroupLabel, table headers, metadata and Badge, 14px minimum for form inputs (16px on touch to avoid iOS zoom), 16px for page titles in the action bar and a dedicated Metric text style (24-32px, tabular-nums, font-medium) for KPI tiles instead of h2; single-line labels at line-height 1.25, multi-line copy at 1.5; controls at h-8 (32px) and Vega/New York geometry, one density shared across all three consoles. Icons: lock iconLibrary to lucide in components.json for all three repos, render nav and table icons at 16px with strokeWidth 1.5 / absoluteStrokeWidth, 12px chevrons and validation glyphs, no per-section coloured icons, aria-label on every icon-only button.
decisions.because: Vercel Geist, GitHub (Mona Sans VF), Atlassian Sans + Mono (GA Sept 2025, slashed zero, ligatures off, 12px floor, dedicated Metric style) and Linear (tuned Inter + Berkeley Mono) replaced bare system stacks with branded sans+mono pairs, and bare Inter is the most-cited generic marker; Primer's 14px medium body / 13px code, Geist's separate Label (single-line, icon-aligned) vs Copy (higher line height) styles, Linear's 13px chrome and shadcn's Nova/Mira dense presets define the 12/13/14/16 band; Vercel's guidelines mandate tabular-nums for compared numbers; Atlassian's 2025 icon refresh moved to 16px/1.5px for density and type harmony and Linear's Mar 2026 refresh reduced and shrank icons; shadcn CLI v4 makes the icon library a config value.

rejected: Two-tier icon rail + secondary panel (Sentry 2025, Datadog, Atlassian flyouts, shadcn sidebar-09): built for multi-product suites with dozens of areas; our largest app has ~20 pages that fit in 6 label-only groups, the rail costs 74px + 190px of width that p95 tables and stack traces need, and keeping rail group counts identical across a 4-group runsheet and a 6-group latchkey would force fake groups.

A distinct sidebar per scope level (Supabase project sidebar, GitLab group/project sidebars): swapping the nav when entering a tenant or project breaks muscle memory and doubles the IA to maintain; Vercel/Sentry-style scope-as-filter keeps one nav and one URL scheme across the three apps.

A shell-level AI chat sidebar or assistant drawer (Grafana Assistant, Datadog Bits chat): the only published usage data (Honeycomb) shows NL querying as an onboarding ramp, not a replacement for structured queries; latchkey's identity/grant/session questions are exact-match and audit-sensitive so a hallucinated 'who has access' answer is a liability. At most a per-object summary card and a palette action in tripline, instrumented before expansion.

Optimistic-by-default mutations everywhere (Linear local-first, Vercel guideline): correct for tripline triage, wrong for latchkey where revoke session, delete tenant, remove grant and rotate secret are security-relevant and often irreversible; those must be blocking modal or typed-name flows, never rolled back from a toast.

Runtime theme generation and user-chosen accents (Linear's base/accent/contrast generator, Radix Themes props): three fixed build-time presets sharing one neutral and differing only in accent is what makes the apps read as one family; a per-user accent picker undermines product recognition and adds a token-validation surface we do not need.

Rich, stacking, promise-driven toasts as the primary feedback channel (shadcn July 2026 Toast): Geist and Primer both scope toasts to acknowledgments; failures of a bulk resolve or a permission denial in a 20-section admin must persist inline, so the shell keeps a deliberately plain Toast and invests in Note/InlineMessage instead.

Zero-radius 'boxy' terminal styling (shadcn Lyra) and the 'anti-generic' cream + serif + terracotta / near-black + acid-green palettes: both are reactions to template fatigue, but sharp corners fight focus rings and nested inputs in dense forms, and editorial palettes make red/amber/green status tokens harder to read; a low-chroma neutral, 6px radius and one accent is the defensible dev-tool register.

Dark-first as a blanket default and light-dark() as the token declaration mechanism: latchkey's admin console is read by support staff in offices and should default to system/light; light-dark() is Baseline 2024 but shadcn's contract, tooling and presets are built on the .dark class remap, so declaring tokens twice per theme stays the cheaper path.

Hidden-by-default (offcanvas) sidebar below 1200px (GitLab Pajamas) and Polaris-style automatic table-to-list collapse on narrow screens: the icon rail already reclaims width, and auto-collapsing tripline's p95 or latchkey's grant tables into list rows hides the comparable columns those tables exist for; only latchkey's incident-time phone use warrants an explicit narrow-screen list fallback, opted in per table.

Row pinning during live streaming (Sentry Logs, Aug 2026) and Atlassian-style 4px line-height grid snapping: the first is a single-vendor feature whose implementation is unverified and only runsheet run logs would use it; the second is one house rule while Primer and Geist use unitless ratios, so it buys nothing for consistency across our three apps.

verified.name: Two-tier shell: narrow icon rail + contextual secondary panel
Collapsible-to-icons sidebar with persisted state and a keyboard toggle is table stakes
Flat groups with label-only headers instead of deep accordions; two levels max, tabs below that
User-curated sidebar: pinned/starred items, hide-and-reorder, and a 'More' overflow
Org/workspace switcher in the sidebar header; sub-scope (project, tenant) as a filter rather than a separate nav tree
Breadcrumbs as the hierarchy indicator in a sticky page action bar (sidebar toggle · breadcrumbs · tabs · actions)
Cmd-K command menu as a navigation layer on top of the sidebar (pages + entities + recent + actions), with explicit discoverability
Density as a named, persisted view setting (not one fixed row height)
Two row primitives: single-line 'list rows' for entity streams, true grid tables for comparable numbers
Tabular numerals + right-aligned numeric columns; monospace only for identifiers
Row detail opens in a resizable right side panel with keyboard prev/next; full pages are reserved for hub entities
Sticky header, frozen leading columns, sticky trailing actions column, and pinned rows as table-level options
Row virtualization for large client-side grids; cursor pagination or 'load newer' for server streams
Restrained inline status: icon+text labels or coloured dots for real state, row tinting for severity, no pills for ordinary metadata
OKLCH as the authoring and derivation space for colour tokens
Two-layer tokens: fixed-role numeric scales underneath, semantic role tokens on top
Accent, brand and status are three separate colour roles; red/amber/green are reserved
Tinted neutrals chosen to match the accent hue
Dark mode as a separately tuned scale, with elevation by lightness and alpha overlays; dark-first is the norm for observability tools
One design system, many products: themes generated from a few inputs and shipped as presets
Contrast baked into the scale, APCA alongside WCAG 2, and colour never carries status alone
Command palette as the action bus (bulk actions, stepwise flows), shipped on by default
List-plus-detail: keyboard row navigation with peek/side-sheet preview, full page for edit forms
Optimistic by default, confirmation scaled to stakes (undo toast -> modal -> typed-name gate)
Toasts demoted to acknowledgments; inline, persistent feedback and explicit-vs-auto save rules
Empty states as a typed set (no-results, blank slate, cleared, permission, error), every screen has a next step
AI moved out of the chat drawer into scoped actions: per-object summaries, palette commands, generated dashboards, and NL search as a layer over structured filters
Agents and automation as visible teammates with status, not as a chatbot; ops work lands in Slack/pager first and the console is the second screen
Branded sans + paired mono replaces the bare system stack (and bare Inter)
Monospace and tabular figures for data columns, IDs and metrics, not only code
The dense-UI type scale: 13-14px body, 12px labels, line-heights snapped to a 4px grid
Low, concentric radius: 4-8px controls, 12px floating surfaces, 'boxy' as the dev-tool dialect
Hairline (often semi-transparent) borders for structure; shadows reserved for floating layers
Iconography: one stroke-style set, 16px with ~1.5px stroke in dense UI, fewer icons overall
Backlash against the default 'AI-generated look' and the shift to codified craft rules
